- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon; apply a 1–2% upward bias for early period (days 1–7).
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction in the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to mean-revert; apply a 1–3% mean-reversion bias toward historical 30-day average for mid-horizon (days 8–15).
- Model tends to ignore sentiment shifts in the last 3–5 days; if sentiment flips sharply, adjust forecast 2–4 days ahead to reflect new sentiment direction.
